verdict: CoreWeave's revenue jumped 420% to $982M in its first quarter as a public company — but $264M of net interest on its datacenter debt and a one-off $177M IPO share-pay charge left a $315M net loss.

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out AI computing power — clusters of Nvidia GPUs in datacenters — to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up 420% YoY as capacity and demand surged.

opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $93M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up from $4M a year ago.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration; up from $16M a year ago, swollen by the one-off $177M IPO share-pay charge (see one-time items).

follow100Note: Interest on the debt that funds CoreWeave's datacenters is the big leak: other expense — mostly $264M of net interest — took $24.57 of every $100 of revenue.
otherDetail: Other expense of $241M net was almost all interest: $264M of net interest expense on the borrowing that funds GPUs and datacenters, partly offset by a $27M gain on fair-value adjustments, less $4M of other expense.
footerNote: CoreWeave reports one segment. Tax was a $46M charge even on a pre-tax loss, driven by its structure and foreign operations.

takeaways.title: Growth exploded in the first public quarter
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 420% to $982M from $189M a year ago, and revenue backlog reached $25.9B — including the $11.2B strategic deal with OpenAI announced in the quarter.

takeaways.title: The cloud itself is profitable before interest
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $606M, a 62% margin, and adjusted operating income was $163M. The GAAP operating loss of $27M includes the one-off $177M IPO share-pay charge.

takeaways.title: Debt costs turned operations into a net loss
takeaways.text: Net interest expense of $264M on the borrowing behind CoreWeave's GPU fleet drove the $315M net loss (EPS -$1.49 diluted), even as demand kept accelerating.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation: $177M of share-pay expense came from awards whose liquidity-event vesting condition was satisfied at CoreWeave's IPO in March 2025 — a one-off spike that sits mostly in general and administrative costs.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Mar 31, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
